The Game of Life was devised by the British Matematician John Horton Conway in 1970.

It's cellular automaton with the following rules:
- if empty cell has 3 neighboors, it becomes live
- if live cell has 2 or 3 neighboors, it remains live
- if live cell has 0, 1 or more than 3 neighboors, it dies and becomes empty
- if empty cell has less or more than 3 neighboors, it remains empty

Here is Game of Life implementation. You could see evolution of random initial configuration.

Control keys:
[p] - pause evolution
[r] - run evolution again
[n] - go to the next evolution step (works when on pause)

You could see current iteration at the top left corner.

21257.d:
A quasi-simulation exploring variations of the antimatter content of a primitive universe,
1 048 576 particles are subjected to the fluctuations of a digital scalar force field.

Each one of the 60 frames per second is a unique generative composition.

(Click ‘open’ to see fullscreen, use wheel/pinch to zoom micro/macro )

-----
* Mint preview *

Minter will get a loopless determinist animation, and a 4320x4320 PNG bitmap.
The "cover" iteration featured here by default uses a 10seconds animation cycle, but new mints will have random animation mode cycles lasting between 1 and 60 seconds. 
To enable the "regular perturbation" mode (10s cycles) please see below "URL modifiers".

-----
* Technics *

This experience is designed to be executed on a recent GPU (>2016) and displayed on 16/9 screens from FHD to 8K+ (1920x1080 → 7680x4320) at 60FPS for infinite duration as the animation scales and creates never-before-seen patterns.

- JavaScript / ThreeJS / WebGL
- Unique generative and determinist animation (animation is seeded by the fxhash mint hash)
- Unlimited duration (no loop) / 6 animations
- 1 second to 1 minute internal algorithm variations

-----
* Controls *

Wheel/pinch : zoom in/out to observe the phenomenon on different scales
Right click + drag : move the observation area
Key "Space" : take a PNG capture of the current view frame (same ratio as window, max 1920x1080)

-----
* URL modifiers *

"&scalartemperature=1400" 
displays the animation with another color.
Colors are expressed in terms of blackbody radiation at a given temperature. Here it will be 1400 Kelvin degrees (~1120°C / 2060°F) corresponding to a lightly hotter than red particles. 
Values accepted in the range 800K to 1 000 000K.

"&perturbation=regular"
allows a regular cycle of animations, each animation mode will be active for 10 seconds

-----
@HAL09999 – November 2022

An ever-growing vortex consisting of lots of different mesh lines that move in unison.

Clicking the canvas will trigger a boost in speed and line size, and produce a random chord by the main synth.

Holding down your pointer will reverse the vortex and play an additional synth on release. Double tapping will have the same effect audio-wise.

This is part of the celebration of fxhash turning 1. That’s why there are 365 editions, and 50% of all primary sales will be donated evenly between “Processing Foundation” and “Three.js”. 20% of all royalties are given back to the minter.

Here are some stats for you:

About 1/10 will render the lines in wireframes.
There are 2 different synth pitches distributed evenly.
10% will have one single line color, instead of 3 primary ones.
In rough measures, every 4th will have an irregular wiggle motion flow instead of a circular one.

In addition to all of the above, there can be different values in regards to line counts, line lengths, line widths, speeds, width grows, radius increments, angle increments, z-index increments, background colors, border colors, and so on.

Features

Parts: the number of symmetrical parts (4|6|8|10)

21274.d:
seq02 is an evolution of seq01. It's a visual/sond sequencer. Each sound/step is represented by a line. The source of line is the target of previous sound. The space where the lines are represented is delimited by an imaginary square, which serves as a border. On each side of the square the range of possible frequencies is mapped, so the final coordinates are on the one hand the limit of the space and the value of the frequency mapped to the imaginary border. The playback order of the sounds is: left->bottom>right->top->left... The first sound/line starts at the left border at an imaginary mapping point, depending on the sustain value of the synth, the line will be represented more or less rapidly towards the next border. When the line of a sound is finished, the next sound is played in the same way.


-Random FEATURES generated by fxrand():

1)num_steps: number of steps/sounds/lines. Can be: 32 (very rare), 48 (rare), 64 (common), 96 (rare), 128 (very rare)

2)color_mode: white (common) or black (rare)

3)line_thikness: 1 (common) or 2 (rare)

4)frequency_range: possible range of frequencies of sounds-> all=45-2500Hz, high-> 1000-2500Hz (rare) and low 45-150 Hz( rare)

5)steps_has_effects: % of sounds/steps that have sound effects (reverb or delay). 

6)x_external_margin: x external margin factor.

7)x_internal_margin: x external margin factor.

8)y_external_margin: y external margin factor.

9)y_internal_margin: y external margin factor.


(The random factor of margins sometimes makes a nice glitch with lines and sounds)


-Other random values generated by fxrand() not included in fxhashFeatures:

1)Frequency of each sound (synth)

2)Velocity of each sound.

2)sustain of each sound.

3)parameters of effects.

4)number of effect lines.

....

----------------------------------

#fxhashturnsone

This work is participating in the FxHash anniversary (#fxhashturnsone) and 100% of the  primary sales go to the Processing Fundation.

Outer mandalas represent the universe or world-system and are traditionally offered as thank you gifts. In this case it’s my offering to the fxhash community as a celebration of #fxhashturnsone. 

SOME MINTS WILL BE GOLDEN TICKETS
A golden ticket AND the iteration directly before it will each receive a free 8 x 10in special edition signed physical made from 12 layers of laser cut museum board. 

Physicals for all mints can be requested and/or claimed at https://alleditions.art

Outer Mandalas is part of a broader series I am working on that explores the use of techniques and patterns from sacred geometries using generative randomness. I use generative algorithms to create “blueprints” that can be transferred out of the physical realm and into the real world as multi-layered three dimensional sculptures. 

I create limited edition physical “prints” for Outer Mandalas by using a high powered laser to precisely cut through 4-ply museum boards (the same stuff you frame a picture with) to create 12 unique layers. I then stack and carefully glue each layer together in order to create a dynamic relief that plays with light and shadow. These pieces are visually engaging artworks that tend to spark conversation whenever they are seen.  

A big thank you to the fxhash platform team and all the passionate collectors and generative artists I’ve met over the past year. It’s been my honor to be a part of this amazing community. 

s to save as a layered SVG 
p to save as a PNG
e to explode the layers
Click and drag the mouse to change the shadows. 

This generative is VERY intensive and probably won’t render very well on a mobile device.

21285.d:
fxhash turns one

Working with text on GEN XYZ Das Occult led me to fooling around with an ascii type project while I worked on those pfps. Gradually that project morphed into this strange hybrid of indie posters, zodiac killer messages and what AI might do to the whole thing. If it were unleashed on it. This collection - I prefer to call my art a collection - includes some palettes inspired by influential fxhash projects as well as mixes of my own.

Themes here can be pretty dark. I've struggled with suicidal ideation in the past and while it seems like it might be a faux pas to put the words suicide and death in these works, I felt I needed to stay true to me and the darkness that tends to walk side by side with the sunny man I often appear to be.

If you struggle with similar issues, please go and speak to someone. It has helped me immensely.

fxhash asked everyone to try and make some donations to worthy causes.

I chose Processing Foundation - since their code work has been so helpful to this community. And to Tezos Ukraine. Because the war there goes beyond the borders of Ukraine and the outcome will have an impact on our global society. If Putin were to succeed... Well he won't with our help.

21287.d:
"Year" is a mere four-letter word. But in reality, much has occurred. There are 12 months or approximately 365 days in a year. I joined fxhash about 4 months ago. And a lot has happened in my life since then. Can you imagine what happened to the people who founded, participated in, and maintained fxhash from its founding days? Everyday must've been different, and each day has its own pattern and color.

I've felt as if I lived in two different worlds since joining fxhash. I'm an architect by day, and a creator by night. I'm a part of fxhash, and I believe every single one of us experiences it that way. Each day has its own pattern and color.

This piece is my way of imagining what this community has gone through in a year. Each block represents a month from November 2021 to October 2022, with every block consists of smaller blocks that represents a day. Each of these days have their own colors and patterns. Every day tells its own story. But when you imagine a bigger picture of what happened in a year, you will see a specific pattern and color that you can keep as one big composition, and that gives you a year full of stories to admire.

I try to participate in the anniversary event as a way of expressing my gratitude. For everyone who has helped build this community so vibrant and meaningful - you have created such a world, and subsequently made my year. And therefore to me, you are all wonderful souls. So many artists, collectors, coders, art enthusiasts, and all of fxhash's teams have inspired me. Don't stop creating awesome stuff. Happy Birthday fxhash!!

This series celebrates fxhash turning one. #fxhashturnsone

I’m so grateful for this place and have ho idea how to adequately articulate how much this platform has changed my life, but it has. A million thanks to the team. You are so appreciated as are the artists and collectors that have made this such a beautiful community. 🥂

Definitely check out “Forever” mode by tapping “F” or mouse click/tap — it will animate (you guessed it) forever and will change its layout every 365 frames, in honor of this wonderful year, and every year after. Some forever modes will “never forget” and others will fade as they progress. No idea if that’s a metaphor but it is a trait, that much I know.

All primary sales are donated to Code/Art, which is a charity that uses “…Art to Inspire Girls in Computer Science.” Read about Code/Art here: https://www.code-art.com/

Ceremony uses public domain art (which is the original, more implicit version CC0) made exclusively by women.

See attached fxtext article for a gallery of the source material and other notes.

Ceremony is also CC0, so feel free use anything here in other projects.

You can read more about CC0 here:
https://creativecommons.org/share-your-work/public-domain/cc0/

F : “Forever” mode (tap after initial render completes)
P : Pause/Play
(mouse click/tap also works to start “Forever” mode or Pause/Play)

A : Add Grain (only works when paused in “Forever” mode.)
G : Toggle Grain (resets the whole piece)
M : Toggle Matte (resets the whole piece)

S : Save Image
1 -> 6 : Set pixel density (resets the whole piece)
(Default pixel density is 1 @ 2000x2000)

If you want to start in "Forever" mode, you can append "&forever=true" to the url in the live view.
You can also add pixel density to the url by appending “&density=2” (or 3, 4, etc) to have it render at higher resolutions by default.

In celebration of #fxhashturnsone, this series speaks to the forms that emerge out of interference patterns. The idea was to study the patterns emerging out of parametric equations and how they might interact. For this, first the space is subdivided and a plan is etched out and on top of which some patterns are layered progressively, creating architectures of interference. In a larger context this work aims to reveal emergent aesthetics on interferences of abstract nature.

#fxhashturnsone - Happy Birthday fxhash!

Some days are busy and some are quiet.
Some weeks go fast and some go slow.
Some months are good, some are bad.
Here we are: talking about, looking at, making, collecting, buying, selling, trading and obsessing about generative crypto art.
Artists, collectors, artworks, opinions, trends, ideas; continuously overlapping, intertwining, influencing, burying, surfacing, remembering and forgetting.
We keep going, in search of the next.

This algorithm draws lines horizontally across the canvas.
There can be 12, 52 or 365 lines.
The lines can be straight, curvy, or both.
Straight lines can be angled or horizontal.
The line thickness can be random from 1-365, or all 12, 52 or 365 pts.
And there are 12 colour palettes.

Inspired by Sol LeWitt’s Wavy Brushstrokes work and the fxhash tweet prompting “365 editions” a week ago.

33% primary & secondary - Processing Foundation.
33% primary & secondary - Waiting To Be Signed podcast

Follow me on twitter/instagram @fauxjebus

~—~—~—~—~—~—~—~—~

F - Fullscreen

21350.d:
Happy birthday fx(hash)!

fx(n-1) is an exploration of building on top of what you've already got.

Each iteration begins with a unique base image.

At each step, we take the current image, draw our base image on top of it, distort this image using a mapping function, and then draw the distorted image on top of our current image.
This combination of previous image + new image is now our new current image, and we repeat the process, varying the parameters to our mapping function as we progress.

Stated more succinctly, at any point in time, our next frame is a function of a mapping function and the currently displayed frame.

This piece is inspired by a paper titled "Symmetric Chaos" by Mike Field and Martin Golubitsky.
My approach towards rendering is rather different, but I'm using the same class of complex equations.

The animation will pause at the same point that the thumbnail is taken, but can be resumed by hitting 'space'. You can also disable the pause by appending ?nopause=true to the URL.

This piece makes heavy use of shaders, and thus (a) may not run well on mobile and (b) has some risk of differences between thumbnail and image based on hardware.

Made with p5.js

Keyboard shortcuts:

'space': play/pause
'h': toggle whether or not we redraw our base image onto the pre-mapped image each frame
's': toggle whether or not we redraw our base image onto the post-mapped image each frame

Ataraxis (or a broken volume renderer) is an exploration in balancing discomfort and calm. The piece generates spaces on the fly that are designed to elicit strange and uncomfortable feelings - like a desolate, alien dreamscape - claustrophobic, surreal, not quite real yet strangely recognisable. But the idea is that while these spaces feel uncomfortable, they're also strangely, antilogically calming. The idea is to elicit a sanguine emotion, to make the viewer feel calm in a strange place, and to lead them somewhere else.

This work is the culmination of many years of work researching volumetric rendering techniques. This token uses a raymarching technique that is intentionally broken in various ways.

Controls:
Double-click to download
&w=X&h=y to change the size of the piece
&dpr=x to change the resolution of the pice - higher resolutions will result in slightly different artworks as the browser attempts to compensate for the overlarge canvas
&fullscreen=true to change the token to display the full size of your browser. This may impact the rendering of the token, so use with caution

21359.d:
Snake Alley is a place in my neighborhood where the sidewalk is narrowly bounded by low-hanging branches on one side and a steep ditch one the other. I have seen countless snakes dart across the sidewalk there at dusk. 

I always wind up at Snake Alley, wearing sandals, at dusk.

This generative system creates unique outputs for each hash. The compositions are organized like spokes through a series of concentric rings, like the Dharmachakra, however these are twisted and centered around an out-spiraling function. Higher-torque versions look more twisted and gnarled, while low-torque versions look like rays emanating from the center.

A number of branches connect each outer ring with its adjacent, inner ring. The layers of branches fill the space with low, medium, or high density - full of circles drawn from the outer layers to the innermost layer. The circles themselves are small or large, within each output.

Fifteen color palettes named after different kinds of snakes were used to lightly color the edges, each drawn with equal likelihood. The titles and colors were adapted from different snake species, typically variants found in the southeastern US, when different colorations occur in other regions. The coral, corn, and milk snakes around Charleston have similar coloration in nature, and their similar color gradients reflect this fact.

I originally composed this artwork in the R Statistics language. I translated the system to p5.js for the one-year anniversary of fxhash. Proceeds from sales will go to Processing.org, the organization that is developing p5.js. #fxhashturnsone 

Verified NFT collectors can purchase a fine art print for their unique token at vadenart.com

About the artist: Kenny Vaden is a generative artist based in Charleston, SC. His art experience included drawing, painting, stained glass apprenticeships, and nature photography. Vaden’s code-based artworks are available online as limited edition or single edition fine art prints, as well as NFTs on Quantum.art, Flamingo DAO Flutter, OpenSea, Objkt, fxhash, and Foundation. More information about the artist and artwork is available on vadenart.com

Painting on canvas using feedback, modulations and noises to recreate the idea of an interactive 'liquid show'. Open livemode, activate your webcam and click on the canvas to start the interaction.
The artwork will adjust to your monitor's resolution but still maintain its aspect ratio.

In commemoration of FXHASH's 1 year anniversary.
You can control some parameters of the video input to adjust the effect with:
1 -> Inverts the brightness values
7/8 -> Increases or decreases the limit on the first parameter
+/- -> Increases or decreases the threshold on the second parameter
P' -> Saves a png from canvas

Designed for desktop computers on Google Chrome
Developed with Hydra.js

21372.d: Chaotic rotation describes the irregular and unpredictable rotation of a spatial body. Unlike Earth's rotation, a chaotic rotation may not have a fixed axis or, indeed, a fixed period. It is easily simulated using a comb and tissue orchestra.

Splits: 
primary -> 10% to processing, 10% to pico_punks breadfond, 40% to #Tezos4Iran donation smart contract, 40% for me
royalties -> 80% for me, 20% for minter

-----------------------
Controls:

F11 -> fullscreen mode (alternatively you should be able to do this from your browser menu)
s -> save a png of the image
1-8 -> set the pixel density and re-render (default is 5, higher means higher resolution final image; the preview image is generated with a value of 5, at 1080x1080px)

-----------------------
Statement: 

For this piece I wanted to explore the Wave Function Collapse algorithm. From the outset, I wanted to implement a version of this where instead of tiles, pixels are used as the basic tiling unit. Instead of discrete edges to connect, the rules for connection are based on HSB values of the pixels. Additionally, instead of minimizing entropy at all times, entropy for each pixel is always increasing, and the pool of possibilities expands rather than contracts (and is randomly selected from). So in short, it's not really Wave Function Collapse, merely inspired by it.

Next, I implemented Entropy Locking, using the same system as in "skyscrapers". Now we can really see the impact that Entropy Locking can have on procedural generation, and how it triggers emergence.

-----------------------

Thanks for reading :)
find my social links, projects, newsletter, roadmap, and more, at aebrer.xyz

license: CC0 -> go nuts; citations not required but definitely appreciated

bonus fact: if the entropy locking method is "none", then the piece should tile on all four edges! try it out!

21417.d:
There are many questions and theories surrounding the magical mechanism of visual perception and how it is linked to our brain processing. 

How much knowledge we learn through perception is based on prior knowledge? 
How much of our perception do we receive directly, and how much do we infer? 

The brain combines external signals when a person explores their environment, leading to the perception of a persistent object. Even though an object is out of sight, it can still be remembered in mind via creative processes. 

When stimuli are spatially and temporally adjacent to one another, they may aggregate perceptually into prominent, coherent patterns or wholes. Our perceptual world is full of what we call a "gestalt, such as when leaves and branches group together to form trees and when trees combine to form forests; when eyes, ears, noses, and mouths arrange themselves into faces; when musical notes combine to form chords and melodies; and when countless dots or pixels come together to form a photograph. Our project is, in a sense challenge of perception, so what do you see? What comes into your mind as a perception when you look at it ??

21419.d:
This generative token continues the Theories of Everything body of work by Phillip David Stearns. The first series of eight works in the Theories of Everything project are physical editions, featuring computationally designed textiles, cut and sewn, and stretched over canvased wood stretchers.

The fabrics of those works and the designs in this generative edition are expressions of algorithms that simulate entropic decay. To a large extent, they are products of code that dutifully and predictably obeys the laws of thermodynamics. Cellular automata, linear feedback shift registers, and pseudo-random number generators execute the binary dance of life and death and the infinite states between. 

It's no coincidence that entropy gives direction to the arrow of time; building layer upon layer of noise upon noise, imbuing our lives with meaning through the churning of endless chaos. Even the universe will experience a death of its own. As its energy disperses, its warmth will fade inevitably to cold; absolute in its stillness.

---

Notes:

- Previews of this work are downsampled and contain a range of unintentional aliasing artifacts. To view these works are intended, please run the work in its own tab or window and press 's' to save a full resolution png.

- Collectors wishing to commission a physical edition of the work may contact the artist directly.

---

Technical Details:

- Each "Theory" is composed of a number of sections within overlapping layers. The maximum number of layers is 4 (rare) and the minimum is 1 (common).

 - Sections contain a single design and a set of binding structures. Designs have one of three formats: solid, gradient, or sampler.

- Solid format designs can be generated from Linear Feedback Shift Register, Random Noise, Cellular Automata, or Pseudoku (a sudoku puzzle generator) design algorithms. Gradients can only be generated using Random Noise. Samplers are only generated using Pseudoku patterns.

- These designs are meant to be woven, so this means they need to be paired with binding structures. Some of the designs are scaled up and paired with structures like opposing twills or satin. Most common is for 8 harness structures to be used.

- Scaling can allow for the structures to be featured more prominently in rendering the designs. Gradient formats are never scaled up always use statin8-7 and satin8-1 for black and white. Samplers are also never scaled up and always use pseudoku generated structures. Depending on the pattern of the design, solid formats can be scaled either 1x, 8x or 9x. 1x scaling always uses the same structures as Gradients. 8x scaling feature either or both twill and or satin structures. 9x will use opposing pseudoku structures.

- Rendering the "Theory" involves rendering each design for each section of each layer. Designs are rendered using their weaving structures based on their scale factor. Each "Theory" is therefore is a complex, and layered weaving.

- The colored "neon" gradient appears only in the top-most layer, and should appear always and only once per "Theory".

I drew my first 8x8 pixel binary image on 11/08/2022 with 'iloveyou' encoded for my wife, it was our 10-year anniversary on this day.  After that made this generative stuff for fxhash's birthday bash.

#fxhashturnsone

Donations:
25% to ThreeJs team

The image contains a binary coded word or phrase with a length of 8 characters. The grays represents 0, the other colors represents 1. One row -> one character. Should be proceed decoding from left to right and from top to bottom.

An example: 'iloveyou'

01101001
01101100
01101111
01110110
01100101
01111001
01101111
01110101

The fxrandom selects a word and the program converts it to binary data. After that, the background (ground and sky) is randomly generated from color schemes. Then the binary gray colors are drawn. Also the color of light next to null colors is randomly generated from color schemes. Random affects also the animation.

The animation stops when you do these interactions below, then restarts after a few seconds of inactivity.

Press spacebar to change:

- frame view -> without frame
- without frame -> original 8x8px size
- original 8x8px size -> frame view

Press 's' to save an svg from current view.

Notes:
- Build with ReactJs and TweenJs
- Every upcoming day, half of the remaining pieces are burned.

The image contains a binary coded word or phrase with a length of 8 characters. The grays represents 0, the other colors represents 1. One row -> one character. Should be proceed decoding from left to right and from top to bottom.

An example: 'iloveyou'

01101001
01101100
01101111
01110110
01100101
01111001
01101111
01110101

The fxrandom selects a word and the program converts it to binary data. After that, the background (ground and sky) is randomly generated from color schemes. Then the binary gray colors are drawn. Also the color of light next to null colors is randomly generated from color schemes. Random affects also the animation.

The animation stops when you do these interactions below, then restarts after a few seconds of inactivity.

- frame view -> without frame

- original 8x8px size -> frame view

Fibonacci tiling of the plane and approximation to Golden Ratio:

Pair 1: 1/1 = 1.000
Pair 2: 2/1 = 2.000
Pair 3: 3/2 = 1.500
Pair 4: 5/3 = 1.6667
Pair 5: 8/5 = 1.6

12 colors added to the Golden Ratio - 20th Century Colors - Modern color palette - 

There were 3 Color Revolutions:

pigment-based paints in oil painting are mostly divided into 3 chronological categories:
	Classic
	Impressionist - 19th century
	Modern - 20th Century 
These 12 colors were perhaps the most significant innovation in the paint industry of the last century.

STRUCTURES

What color do things look when you're happy?

First of all I want to dedicate this collection to all the people who paint their emotions with color, who through a chromatic range, are capable of feeling a universe of sensations most of the time inexplicable.....

 I am fascinated by how generative art creates a perfect symbiosis between art and technology, allowing through a set of algorithmic rules to give rise to compositions where shapes and colors coexist in balance, harmonized with each other that give rise to new creations.

This collection is designed to be self-contained and limited, recreating the view from different angles and phases of the day that can lead to disparate interpretations of a piece.

My work as a visual artist explores elements such as randomness and chance of linear formations and geometric gradients that broaden the spectrum to increasingly new concepts that I definitely want to explore.

I continually wonder what the geometric patterns that will emerge from my sensibility will be like and will give rise to new collections like this one, which is why I continue to investigate techniques and shapes while having fun.

"A painting is not the image of an experience, but it is the experience." Mark Rothk

We would do it all summer long on the campus of the University of Bochum in Germany. I felt completely safe, not least because my father worked in his lab a few minutes away. Jumping and almost flying high through air doesn't come naturally to many. There is insecurity in having both feet off the ground, like falling in a dream, or hanging in midair. I craved this moment of zero gravity at the peak of the jump, the closest to flying I could get.

I photographed the concrete blocks with an iPhone, drew the characters digitally by hand and made the background with p5.js

Continuing on the theme of color perception in Farbteiler, Punktwelt is an exploration of color interaction, projection and perceived depth, and the aesthetics of simple Boolean operations on form.

Each shape is the result of a single block, a rectangular cuboid, subjected to a series of Boolean subtractions with other blocks, and rendered in parallel projection, oblique or axonometric, in the abstract landscape of the Punktwelt.

Some have horizons, some have banded or striped backgrounds. The unnatural drawing order and chromatic differences of the individual faces sometimes yields illusory or paradoxical visual geometries.

Press ’s’ to save a png. Press ’4’ to export a high resolution png. Press ’8’ to export a very high resolution png. Press ’e’ to export an SVG file (may take some time and produce large files).

Aspect ratio variations are 4:5, 5:4, 2:3, 3:2 and 1:1.

Built in Javascript with p5.js, p5.svg and csg.js.

Asterium is a token that will grow with you, for an entire year. Changing and morphing over time to eventually reach its equilibrium.

It is a token where I try to symbolize the journey of life.
Where looking back is the best way to look forward.
Where looking into the future is not a possibility.
Where each day is as uncertain as the next.

A token that will surprise you and have its ups and downs as it grows over time.



Pricing:
Dutch auction 64-16-8, where anybody that picks one up at 64 tez gets a print of how their galaxy looks on any day from the present to day 0. Meaning you can claim the print at any point in the future.

The print will be printed on high quality hahnemühle torchon paper at 30x40 cm (11.81 x 15.75 in). Printed at a local print shop here in Utrecht. This paper has a rough texture to it that matches the textures of space perfectly.



Usage:
- Hover over your Asterium to view the name, date, days passed, status and render stats.
- Double press to export the current frame as a .png image.
- Use the slider at the bottom to scroll back in time to the days before today, you can go as far back as day 0 and as far forwards as today.
- The token refreshes every hour, so framing it in a digital picture frame is totally possible!
